title: TSMC To Commence A14 Process Node Mass Production in the First Half of 2028, Eyeing a 7.5x Capacity Versus Intel’s 14A and Scaling SRAM After Almost A
gist: TSMC is reportedly preparing A14 mass production in 1H 2028, with possible 7.5x Intel 14A capacity and SRAM bit-cell shrinkage after roughly eight years. The article stresses that only the 2028 schedule and performance targets are official.

insights.claim: TSMC is reportedly preparing to start A14 mass production in the first half of 2028, tightening official guidance that says only 2028 volume production.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Reported, not confirmed; a first-half date would pull forward revenue contribution.

insights.claim: DigiTimes via Wccftech reports TSMC could have 7.5 times Intel's 14A manufacturing capacity in 2028, a projection not a confirmed outcome.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Capacity asymmetry would favor TSMC for large customer launches; treat as unverified.
insights.locator: That comparison remains a reported projection

insights.claim: A14 uses TSMC's second-generation nanosheet transistors, offering 10-15% higher speed at the same power or 25-30% lower power at the same speed versus N2.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Official node gains frame the upgrade case for leading-edge customers.

insights.claim: TSMC targets more than 20% higher logic density on A14, supported by its NanoFlex Pro architecture.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Density gains drive cost per transistor for AI and CPU designs.

insights.claim: Electronic Times reports A14 could shrink high-density SRAM bit cells below 0.017 square micrometers, from about 0.021 since N5, ending roughly eight years of stalled scaling.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: If true, larger caches fit per die for CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators; a rare SRAM scaling gain.

insights.claim: Exact first-half launch, capacity multiple and SRAM dimensions require further confirmation, and yields, costs and customer adoption will determine competitive outcome.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Discount the headline numbers until confirmed; watch yields and customer tape-outs.
insights.locator: the distinction between official targets and industry reporting
